summaryBox.title: Decarboxylation & HVZ Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: Soda-lime (NaOH/CaO) yields alkane with 1 less carbon. HVZ (X₂/Red P) selectively α-halogenates acids with ≥1 α-H; fails for HCOOH and (CH₃)₃C-COOH.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DECARBOXYLATION PATHWAYS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  SODA-LIME DECARBOXYLATION                               KOLBE'S ELECTROLYSIS
  $R\text{COONa} + \text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\text{CaO}, \Delta} \mathbf{R\text{-H}} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ $2 R\text{COONa} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Electrolysis}} \mathbf{R\text{-}R} + 2\text{CO}_2$
  (Yields alkane with **1 carbon less**).                  (Anodic free radical coupling).

HELL-VOLHARD-ZELINSKY (HVZ) REACTION:
R-CH₂-COOH + X₂ ──[1. Red P, 2. H₂O]──► R-CH(X)-COOH (α-Halo Acid) + HX
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Soda-Lime Decarboxylation**: $R\text{COONa} + \text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\text{CaO}, \Delta} R\text{-H} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$.
- **Kolbe Electrolysis**: Electrolysis of sodium carboxylate produces symmetrical alkane at anode via radical dimerization.
- **HVZ Reaction**: Carboxylic acids with $\alpha$-H react with $\text{Cl}_2$ or $\text{Br}_2$ and Red Phosphorus followed by water to yield $\alpha$-halo carboxylic acids. Fails for Formic acid ($\text{HCOOH}$) and Trimethylacetic acid ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-COOH}$) due to lack of $\alpha$-hydrogens.

conceptBreakdown.title: 9. 10 High-Yield NEST Traps & Master Glossary
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
10 NEST ALDEHYDES, KETONES & CARBOXYLIC ACIDS TRAPS SUMMARY

1. NaBH₄ CANNOT reduce carboxylic acids or esters (LiAlH₄ required).
2. Benzaldehyde FAILS to reduce Fehling's or Benedict's solution.
3. In semicarbazide, ONLY the -NH₂ attached to -NH- is nucleophilic.
4. In crossed Cannizzaro (PhCHO + HCHO), Formaldehyde is EXCLUSIVELY OXIDIZED.
5. Clemmensen uses conc. HCl (cleaves -OH, ethers); use Wolff-Kishner instead.
6. Formic acid (HCOOH) gives POSITIVE Tollens' and Fehling's tests!
7. Trimethylacetic acid lacks α-hydrogens and FAILS the HVZ reaction.
8. Almost ALL o-substituted benzoic acids are STRONGER ACIDS than Benzoic Acid (Ortho-Effect).
9. Popoff's rule: keto group stays with the SMALLER alkyl group during oxidation.
10. Aldol requires AT LEAST ONE α-hydrogen (otherwise Cannizzaro occurs).
